assessment.summary: BRAF is one of the most extensively validated oncology drug targets, with 5 approved small-molecule inhibitors, over 11,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, 138 PDB structures (best resolution 1.5Å), and more than 7,300 publications. The target is highly druggable with a well-characterised ATP-binding pocket and multiple clinical-stage compounds. Resistance mechanisms (e.g., V600E mutation, paradoxical MAPK activation) are well-documented but have been addressed by next-generation inhibitors.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT of 66.4 (55% high-confidence fraction) suggests disordered regions outside the kinase domain are not well-modelled, though this does not affect druggability of the kinase domain itself
Structural and chemical data are heavily focused on the V600E mutant and ATP-competitive inhibitors; allosteric and non-kinase-domain binding sites are less characterised
Resistance mechanisms (paradoxical ERK activation, splice variants, RAS-independent dimerisation) remain incompletely addressed by current approved agents
Efficacy data in non-melanoma, non-thyroid tumour types (e.g., colorectal cancer) is limited due to intrinsic resistance, and the mechanistic basis is not fully resolved
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for newer-generation inhibitors are not comprehensively reported in public databases
